propositions: Code review has no detection language for checks whose PASS/absent/empty result is indistinguishable from the check never having run, appearing at least 12 times in calibration (9 test-oracle and shipped-code instances; 1 mirror case of false-positive alarm)

A check that verifies absence using grep/regex over tool output or subprocess output with no producer-liveness check (exit status, non-empty capture, presence assertion) produces fail-open verdicts indistinguishable from producer failure

The same defect pattern has an inverse: a check reporting a confident FAIL (e.g., missing artifacts) for a reason other than the condition it verifies, producing false alarms as damaging as false passes

Fail-open language must be added to the existing tests criterion (oracle antipattern in code-review-tests.md) and error-handling criterion (shipped-code patterns in code-review-base.md) rather than creating a new criterion
Calibration replay of 9 pre-fix seeded diffs must yield ≥1 finding per case naming the producer-liveness defect, and 9 post-fix corrected diffs must yield zero findings
User-facing documentation of the fail-open pattern and producer-liveness litmus must be added to the rebar explain review guide with ≥2 worked examples from the corpus
